newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Excite CEO targets advertising.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Excite CEO targets advertising.

text.p: Excite Inc Chief Executive Officer George Bell said on Monday the company hoped to use its status as America Online Inc's exclusive Internet search service to expand its share of advertising on the World Wide Web.

One of the company's top three objectives for 1997 "is to be number one on the Web in terms of advertising revenues and advertising innovations," Bell told Reuters in an interview after the announcement of Excite's agreement with AOL.
Bell said he expected Excite's acquisition of AOL's WebCrawler search service to be positive for cash flow.
"The transaction is cash flow positive to us right away, revenues exceed expenses," he said in a telephone conference.
"We believe that consolidation will continue to take place in the search and directory marketplace," Bell told Reuters.

A key part of the deal, according to Bell and industry analysts, is the ability to snap up the tremendous market reach of WebCrawler, which as a primary tool of AOL's seven million subscribers accessing the Internet is ranked number two in search market reach behind rival Yahoo! Inc.
PC-Meter, which provides independent tracking of Web use among home users, gives WebCrawler a 29.2 percent reach.

This figure, drawn from the most recent data in September, compares with a rating of 39.3 percent for Yahoo! and 19.2 percent for Excite itself. Rivals Infoseek Corp and Lycos Inc have 18.8 and 17.7 percent, respectively.

Aside from AOL and Netscape Communications Corp, the Internet software pioneer whose Web site has long been the most heavily-trafficked on the World Wide Web, the search and navigation firms effectively top the most visited sites.
The combined network of Excite and WebCrawler would have a unduplicated reach of 44.1 percent, according to a market analysis conducted for Excite by PC-Meter.

"If you're going to reach broad audiences and access large numbers of people, the search engines are the place to be after AOL and Netscape," PC-Meter vice president Pamela Smith said of the Internet advertising market.

Bell noted that AOL's Interactive Advertising group will sell all the advertising appearing on the co-branded AOL - Excite search facility in a deal that is exclusive for two years, with a further deal extendable for three more years.
"The majority of that revenue goes to AOL and the minority of that revenue goes to Excite," he said, without elaborating.
"We expect for that to be a pretty significant revenue contributor going forward," Bell added.

Shares of Excite rose as high as 9-3/4 on Nasdaq, valuing the WebCrawler deal as high as $19 million at one point, before settling at nine -- up 2-7/8 -- while America Online gained 1-1/2 to 32-5/8 in New York Stock Exchange trade.

"We're describing the new network, with WebCrawler in it, as a network that's doing between 10 and 12 million page views on a daily basis," said Bell. This compares with the 14 million in average daily page views Yahoo reported in September and somewhere around four million for other rivals.

With the current practice of using so-called banner advertisements, in which companies provide a graphical band on which a user can click to go to an advertiser's site, each page represents an opportunity for advertisements.
"What this does for me is it creates a sufficient amount of inventory," said Bell. "The challenge that I face in 1997 is quite clear, which is to do a great job in advertising."

Bell and other Internet advertising executives expect significant changes in advertising format next year, with new innovative features like sponsorship sections and greater use of multimedia capabilities.

WebCrawler is the second major acquisition in the Internet search and navigation space. Excite also drove the previous consolidation move this summer when it purchased The McKinley Group in a deal estimated at around $16 million.

"I do not plan to support three big brands for a lot longer," said Bell, noting McKinley's Magellan primarily offered strong editorial product, while WebCrawler has "the early-mover advantage Yahoo has, but not as much sex appeal."
Bell said Excite's aggressive acquisitions were aimed at making sure it has "the privilege of playing in the finals" of the race to be top Internet brand in the future.
-- sam.perry@reuters.com, Palo Alto Bureau _1 415 846 5400
